I’m an old hand at this, and I don’t farm by fancy numbers. I look at what my land did before, what I can pay for, and whether the family has enough hands at the busy time. This year I will still keep most of my land in cotton, because cotton is what I know best and it brings cash if the year is decent. But I won’t put everything into one thing. I keep some wheat and maize, and a little mungbean, so if cotton price is bad or weather turns against me, I still have grain and some money coming in. Money is tight because some people work away and can’t always help at the right time, so I won’t push inputs too hard. I’d rather do what has worked on my fields: enough fertilizer so the crop doesn’t go hungry, a few well irrigations when the crop really needs water, and not too much hired labor unless I have no choice.

For wheat, the crop is already in the field from last autumn, so now I will mainly watch water and topdressing. If the leaves stay green and we get a bit of spring rain, I won’t spend too much extra. For cotton, I will plant on the bigger share of land because that is my main cash crop. I’ll use the seed people around here commonly buy, not the most expensive one. For maize, I’ll keep a small area, mainly because it is dependable and the family can use it. Mungbean I plant on a small piece because it doesn’t need as much money and it helps spread risk. I have well water, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate just because I can. I will save water for the key times.
